Day 1 / CorgiMind

I’m Asaf Saar.

I run CorgiMind, where I build things with AI and show how I test them.

  • I still own an original Commodore 64. Today it’s our target machine.
  • I’ll drive the keyboard. If a command flies by, ask me to stop and explain it.
Day 1 / CorgiMind

Tank’s Disk Rescue

Tank the corgi explores a collapsed computer archive. Dig a route to the lost disks, collect them and reach the exit.

  • The choice, inspired by Boulder Dash: take a shortcut under a heavy crate, or dig around it?
  • Today’s slice: one room, one pickup, ten points. D collects. R resets.
PowerShell

What’s on this machine?

Start in a clean Windows 11 VM. Check the OS, WinGet and which tools are already installed.

Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption, OSArchitecture
winget --version
Get-Command git,claude,cl65,x64sc -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name,Source
PowerShell

Install Claude Desktop

Open the official Windows download in the VM. Run the installer. When Claude opens, leave the sign-in screen there while you install the CLI.

Start-Process 'https://claude.com/download'
PowerShell

Install the Claude Code CLI

In Windows PowerShell, run the installer from Anthropic. When it finishes, open a fresh PowerShell window.

irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
Claude Desktop

Sign in to Claude Desktop

Switch capture to the C64. Open Claude from Start and sign in with your Claude Code-enabled account. Once you see a new chat ready for input, leave Desktop open.

PowerShell

Sign in to Claude Code

Keep sign-in off camera. In the new PowerShell window, verify the CLI version and launch browser sign-in. Choose the same account you used in Desktop.

claude --version
claude auth login
PowerShell

Verify both sessions

Check that Desktop opens a new chat. Run this PowerShell check to show the CLI result without displaying account details. Return capture to the VM once both checks pass.

claude auth status | Out-Null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Claude Code sign-in is incomplete' }
Write-Host 'Claude Code is signed in.'
PowerShell

Install Git

With both Claude sessions ready, install Git for version control. Read the installer prompts, then reopen PowerShell.

winget install --id Git.Git --exact --source winget
PowerShell

Check the development tools

Verify Git and run the Claude Code diagnostic before creating the game repository.

git --version
claude doctor
PowerShell

Create the project

The demo email is scoped to this repository. Run the remaining commands from this folder.

$project = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'source\tank-disk-rescue'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $project | Out-Null
Set-Location $project
git init
git config --local user.name "Asaf Saar"
git config --local user.email "asaf@corgimind.invalid"
PowerShell

Start Claude Code

Launch the signed-in CLI from your new game repository.

claude
Claude prompt

Plan the first observable result

Read Claude’s three acceptance checks together before approving any edit.

We are live on a clean Windows 11 machine, in an empty Git repo. Our eventual game is Tank’s Disk Rescue for an original Commodore 64. Today’s experiment is tiny: display Tank beside one floppy disk, press D to collect it, and see the score change from 0 to 10 exactly once. R resets the scene. We will use cc65 and VICE. Give me a three-step plan and three things a human must observe to call this a success. Wait for my approval before creating files.
Claude Code

Return to PowerShell

Leave the interactive Claude session to install the C64 tools.

/exit
PowerShell

Prepare two download paths

cc65 targets the Commodore processor. VICE runs the result on Windows.

$tools = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'C64Tools'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $tools | Out-Null
$ccZip = Join-Path $tools 'cc65.zip'
$viceZip = Join-Path $tools 'vice.zip'
PowerShell

Download cc65 and VICE

Use the rehearsed archives. If a mirror fails, save the official ZIPs at the same two paths.

curl.exe -fL --retry 2 -o $ccZip 'https://downloads.sourceforge.net/project/cc65/cc65-snapshot-win32.zip'
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'cc65 download failed' }
curl.exe -fL --retry 2 -o $viceZip 'https://downloads.sourceforge.net/project/vice-emu/releases/binaries/windows/GTK3VICE-3.10-win64.zip'
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'VICE download failed' }
PowerShell

Verify and extract

Compare both hashes with the rehearsal copies. Keep the full extracted directories.

Get-FileHash $ccZip,$viceZip | Format-List Path,Hash
Expand-Archive -LiteralPath $ccZip -DestinationPath "$tools\cc65" -ErrorAction Stop
Expand-Archive -LiteralPath $viceZip -DestinationPath "$tools\vice" -ErrorAction Stop
PowerShell

Find the tool binaries

Run in the same PowerShell session. If you reopen it, repeat this slide and the next one.

$tools = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'C64Tools'
$cc = Get-ChildItem "$tools\cc65" -Filter cl65.exe -Recurse | Select-Object -First 1
$vice = Get-ChildItem "$tools\vice" -Filter x64sc.exe -Recurse | Select-Object -First 1
if (!$cc -or !$vice) { throw 'Expected cl65.exe and x64sc.exe inside extracted archives' }
PowerShell

Start the emulator

Look for the C64 BASIC READY prompt. Close VICE after this check.

$env:Path = "$($cc.DirectoryName);$($vice.DirectoryName);$env:Path"
Set-Location (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'source\tank-disk-rescue')
cl65 --version
Start-Process -FilePath $vice.FullName
PowerShell

Return to Claude

Launch from the project folder. Review the proposed main.c edit on screen.

claude
Claude prompt

Build a one-pickup game

Look for the variable that remembers whether the pickup is still available.

Create only main.c in the current project. Write a small C89 program for cc65's C64 target using conio.h. Show the original title TANK'S DISK RESCUE, a tiny bordered room, a T for Tank, and one * immediately to his right for a disk. Include a visible legend, SCORE 0, D = RIGHT and R = RESTART. Use distinct readable colors and keep every line inside 40 columns. Wait for a key with cgetc(). Accept both key cases as appropriate to cc65 on C64. On the first D, move Tank into the disk cell, remove the disk, and show SCORE 10. Further D presses leave the room and score unchanged. R restores the original positions and score. Other keys leave state unchanged. After every change wait for input again. Use simple portable code and explain how the pickup can only score once. End after writing the source so I can review and build it on camera.
Claude Code

Leave the coding session

Review the source before compiling.

/exit
PowerShell

Read and compile main.c

Read the first compiler diagnostic if the build fails.

Get-Content .\main.c
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\build | Out-Null
cl65 -t c64 -O -o .\build\rescue.prg .\main.c
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Build failed. Read the first compiler diagnostic.' }
PowerShell

Identify and launch the PRG

Show the filename, size and SHA-256. Launch those bytes in VICE.

Get-Item .\build\rescue.prg | Select-Object Name,Length,LastWriteTime
Get-FileHash .\build\rescue.prg -Algorithm SHA256
& $vice.FullName -autostart (Resolve-Path .\build\rescue.prg).Path
Day 1 / CorgiMind

Try to score twice

Click VICE to give the emulator keyboard focus.

  • Launch, then press X. Tank and the disk stay in place. Score 0.
  • Tap D. Tank takes the disk. Score 10.
  • Press D twice more. The score stays at 10.
  • Tap R. The disk returns and the score resets. Tap D to collect it again.
PowerShell

Bring the evidence back

Close VICE and open Claude in the project folder. Choose the next prompt based on what you saw.

claude
Claude prompt

If the test failed

Reproduce the failure twice. Replace the bracketed fields with the actual keys and results before sending.

I ran the current PRG in VICE. My input sequence was [keys]. I expected [visible result]. I actually saw [visible result], twice. Inspect main.c, name the smallest state or input-handling change that explains this, then make that one fix. Give me the exact retest sequence. I will run it and report the observation.
Claude prompt

If the test passed

Compare the code trace with the observed emulator run. After an edit, rebuild and repeat the same keys.

Read main.c. Trace D, D, R, D starting from launch. List the expected score and disk state after each key. Mark this as a code trace. Ask me for my VICE observations and leave the physical C64 result pending.
Claude prompt

Save the verified workflow

Review the proposed files. Exit Claude with /exit before running the next PowerShell block.

Put our verified compile command in build.cmd. Have it run from its own folder, create build if needed, return a nonzero exit on compile failure, and show the generated PRG size on success. Add .claude/skills/c64-build/SKILL.md with the name c64-build and a description. Its instructions should run build.cmd from the project root, stop on failure, report the path, byte size and SHA-256 of the successful PRG, and leave emulator/hardware playtests for the presenter. Add a short CLAUDE.md documenting the target, controls, build command, and separate compile, emulator and physical test results. Add a .gitignore for build/ and *.o. Preserve main.c. Show me the files before executing anything.
PowerShell

Inspect the project instructions

Check the build script, the skill and Claude’s project notes.

Get-Content .\build.cmd
Get-Content .\.claude\skills\c64-build\SKILL.md
Get-Content .\CLAUDE.md
PowerShell

Build again and restart Claude

Check the exit code and hash before starting a fresh Claude session.

.\build.cmd
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Stop before loading the PRG' }
Get-FileHash .\build\rescue.prg -Algorithm SHA256
claude
Claude Code

Invoke the project skill

Inspect the reported path, size and hash. Leave the session with /exit. If time is tight, open Day 2 here.

/c64-build
PowerShell

Identify the transfer media

Use this route only for a rehearsed loader with removable storage. Confirm the actual mounted folder.

Get-Volume | Format-Table DriveLetter,FileSystemLabel,DriveType,SizeRemaining
$media = Read-Host 'Enter the existing folder on your C64 media (example E:\)'
if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $media -PathType Container)) { throw 'Media folder missing' }
PowerShell

Copy and verify the same bytes

Use a fresh destination. After the hashes match, eject the media through Windows.

$copy = Join-Path $media 'RESCUE.PRG'
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $copy) { throw 'Choose an empty folder for this rehearsal' }
Copy-Item -LiteralPath .\build\rescue.prg -Destination $copy -ErrorAction Stop
if ((Get-FileHash $copy).Hash -ne (Get-FileHash .\build\rescue.prg).Hash) { throw 'Copy mismatch' }
C64 BASIC

Load on the original C64

For a mounted disk on device 8, use the exact directory entry. If it is RESCUE.PRG, include the extension. With a cartridge browser, select the PRG there.

LOAD"RESCUE",8,1
RUN
